name: X (Formerly Twitter)
tagline: A global public timeline where people post short things and argue about them.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely build the software. A microblog with posts, follows, likes, replies and a reverse-chronological feed is a textbook one-session build, and an agent will hand you a working one with tests. What you cannot build is the several hundred million other people who are already there, which is the entire product. A personal X clone is a diary with a like button, useful maybe as a self-hosted notes stream, worthless as a replacement for reading what a stranger in another country said about a news event twenty seconds ago. The consolation build below is a personal posting and archive tool, not a substitute.
coreLoopDIY: Runs a local microblog where you post short entries, follow RSS and ActivityPub accounts, and read one merged reverse-chronological timeline.
requirements: A machine or small VPS to run it on
Optional: a domain if you want your posts publicly readable
Optional: X API access if you want to mirror posts out, which is neither cheap nor stable
whatYouLose: The audience: nobody follows your self-hosted timeline
Real time breaking news and the crowd reacting to it
Search across everyone else's posts, which is most of the actual utility
DMs, quote tweets of people you do not host, and the ambient sense of what is happening
Moderation and spam handling, which you now own personally
moatNotes: Every feature is copyable in an afternoon. The graph is not. Multiple well-funded, technically competent clones have proven this repeatedly.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay X for reach, a checkmark, longer posts and fewer ads, but they use X because everyone else does. That is the whole thing. Journalists, sports fans, traders and shitposters are all standing in the same room, and no amount of local software puts you in that room. Even the well-built alternatives with real funding and real apps struggle here, which should tell you what a weekend project is up against.
notes: The client is a one-sitting build and always has been. The moat is a few hundred million people already standing in the same room, plus the archive of everything they said.
prompt:
Build a single-user, self-hosted microblog and reading client called "Timeline". This is a personal posting and reading tool, not a social network.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20 with TypeScript
- Fastify for the HTTP server
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/timeline.db
- Server-rendered HTML with Eta templates plus a little vanilla JS, no React, no build step for the frontend
- Vitest for tests

In scope:
1. Posting: a compose box, posts up to 5000 chars, Markdown rendered to HTML and sanitized, optional image upload stored on disk under ./data/media with a thumbnail.
2. Threads: a post can reply to another post; render threads nested one level deep.
3. Following external sources: a subscriptions table holding RSS/Atom feed URLs and Mastodon/ActivityPub account URLs (fetch their public .rss feed, do not implement the ActivityPub protocol).
4. A poller that fetches all subscriptions every 15 minutes, dedupes by GUID, stores items, and respects ETag/Last-Modified.
5. One merged reverse-chronological timeline of my own posts plus subscription items. No algorithm, no ranking, no engagement scores.
6. Full text search over everything using SQLite FTS5.
7. Tags parsed from #hashtags in my posts, with a per-tag view.
8. Public read-only mode: if PUBLIC_MODE=true, unauthenticated visitors can read my own posts only, never the subscription firehose.
9. Export: GET /export returns a JSON dump of all my posts and media paths.
10. Auth: single admin password from .env, hashed session cookie. No user accounts, no OAuth, no signup flow.

Out of scope, do not build: likes, follower counts, notifications, DMs, recommendations, ads, moderation tooling, mobile apps, X API integration, any telemetry.

Requirements:
- .env for ADMIN_PASSWORD, SESSION_SECRET, PORT, PUBLIC_MODE. Ship .env.example, never commit .env.
- Idempotent SQL migrations run at boot.
- Tests for the feed parser, dedupe logic, Markdown sanitization and search.
- README with setup in under ten lines and one honest paragraph stating this replaces personal posting and reading, not a social graph.
- Seed script that inserts three sample posts and two real public RSS feeds so the timeline is not empty on first run.
